description: The kind of one control in a device profile (DESIGN v2.7 A): button, axis or key. The obsolete pre-v2.7 value hold reads as button, and is never written back (encoding writes the kind's own name). Any other string fails the control, and with it the profile. Input is the kind string as a profile file holds it; expected is the kind it reads as, or null when it fails.
function: ControlDescriptor.Kind decoding — input the kind string, expected "button", "axis", "key" or null
verifiedBy: DESIGN.md v2.7 A; Tests/PowerUpTests/DeviceFixtureTests.swift testControlKindTable decodes a ControlDescriptor holding the kind and reads its raw value. Rust: rust/powerup-core/tests/device.rs control_kind_cases runs profile::ControlKind::from_wire.

cases.name: button
cases.reason: A control that is pressed and released.

cases.name: axis
cases.reason: A control with a continuous value (v2.7 A).

cases.name: the pre-v2.7 hold reads as a button
cases.reason: Whether an action holds belongs to the action, so a profile written before v2.7 must not fail on its obsolete hold kind (HK-005).

cases.name: kinds are case-sensitive
cases.reason: Button is not button; an unknown kind fails the control.

cases.name: hold is matched exactly
cases.reason: Only the exact legacy spelling is read as a button.

cases.name: an unknown kind fails
cases.reason: A kind this build does not know fails the control rather than guessing.

cases.name: an empty kind fails
cases.reason: An empty string is not a kind.
